evidence: Traupman 333: prō vītā cautiō, life insurance
M-O s.v. insurance: life insurance, vītae cautiō (after Egger)
terms.comment: Classically a bond or security given against loss (Cic. Fam. 7.18.1; Lewis & Short); Traupman and Egger use it for insurance.

evidence: Traupman 333: assēcūrātiō vehiculāria, car insurance; assēcūrātiō valētūdināria, health insurance
terms.comment: From sēcūrus; not in Lewis & Short.

terms.gloss: be insured: avoid a loss for an agreed fee

phrases.latin: quōrum duo postulāta fuēre, ūnum ut mīlitiā vacārent dum in eō pūblicō essent, alterum ut quae in nāvēs imposuissent ab hostium tempestātisque vī pūblicō perīculō essent
phrases.english: They made two demands: first, that they be free of military service while on this public contract; second, that whatever they put on board should be at the state’s risk against the enemy and storms

phrases.latin: Nam et negōtiātōribus certa lucra prōposuit susceptō in sē damnō, sī cui quid per tempestātēs accidisset
phrases.english: He offered merchants a sure profit, taking the loss upon himself if storms brought anyone to grief

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 333, checked against the searchable text of the book (9 November 2026).
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. insurance: life insurance; insurance company.
Enrico Levi and Arturo Bini, Il latino come lingua viva (1937), p. 7 (assicurazione).
Livy and Suetonius checked against the Latin Library texts (CLTK mirror) (9 November 2026).
